chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Sayf, from Manṣūr al-Ṣayqal, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man was affected by janābah during the night, so he performed ghusl. Then when morning came, he looked and found janābah on his garment. He said: Praise be to Allah, who has not left anything except that it has a limit. If, when he got up, he looked and did not see anything, then there is no repetition upon him. But if, when he got up, he did not look, then repetition is upon him.

key_terms.إِعَادَةَ: repetition of the act, here meaning repeating the prayer
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: an expression of praise to Allah at the clarification of the ruling
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment, the clothing in which he prayed
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: major ritual impurity caused here by sexual defilement
key_terms.حَدٌّ: a defined limit or boundary in the law
key_terms.نَظَرَ: he examined or checked for impurity

ai.seo_question: If someone performs ghusl and later finds impurity on his garment, must he repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about praying in a garment later found to have najasah from janābah. If the person had checked and did not see anything, there is no need to repeat; but if he failed to check, he must repeat. It highlights attentiveness to taharah and that the law distinguishes between due care and negligence.
